title: Configuring a Scale
titles: Configuring a Scan and Weigh Device
breadcrumbs: Configuring a Scan and Weigh Device

children:
You will use this window to configure  
 various settings that define how a scale and the system will communicate with 
 each other. The application requires a separate scale for each packing station. This configuration applies to any user using the machine where the config file is installed. Note that you can use the Delete 
 Configuration Values option (on the Actions Menu) to 
 erase a user's previously-saved configuration values from the system.

Apply Button: When the Generate config file setting is unchecked, it saves the data to the individual user’s user.config file (not the registry).  When the setting is checked, it generates the config file.

OK Button: This button 
 performs the same functions as the Apply Button, except that it will also 
 exit the Scale Configuration Window (unless an error was found).

Cancel Button: This button 
 will close the Scale Configuration Window, losing all user changes that 
 were made in the current, unsaved session.

NOTE: When the workstation is configured to use RemoteApp or RDP to access a server and run the web browser from there (such as when using virtualization software), the scale must be set up to communicate to the screen via "wedge" software. This is software that takes the output of the device and sends it to the cursor on the screen, as if it were entered on the keyboard. In this situation, the user must have the cursor on the weight field at the time of placing the container on the scale. The Scale configuration is not used at all in this setup.

Click on a link 
 below to view procedures:

The first step in scale setup is to attach the device to your machine. 
 Most scales are attached to the serial (COM) port located at the back 
 of your computer. You will need check to see if your machine's COM port 
 is currently active. You can do this in the Windows Control Panel. See 
 your Windows help system, your scale manual, or your system consultant 
 for any specific questions on activating COM ports. After plugging in the device, the system will notify you about which COM port is used.

For the scale and computer to have a proper connection, you will need 
 to define the scale's technical settings on the Connection Properties 
 Tab.Most of the values you should 
 enter in these fields are in your scale's instruction manual. Ask your 
 system consultant if you have any further questions

Access the Scale 
 Configuration Window (accessed from the desktop), and click on 
 the Connection Properties Tab.

Use the COM Port Field to 
 choose the serial port to which you are going to attach your scale.

Use the Scale Connection Properties 
 fields to define your serial connection:

Baud Rate: This field 
 represents the connection speed.

Bits Per Byte: This 
 field represents the number of bits used to represent the character being 
 transmitted. The receiver (the system) and the transmitter (the scale) 
 must agree on the number of data bits. Almost all devices transmit data 
 using 7 or 8 bits. See the scale manual for the setting for your scale.

Parity: This field 
 specifies the type of parity to be used on the port connection. Parity 
 is used to detect data corruption during transmission.

Stop Bits: After a 
 character has been transmitted (in the number of bits defined in the Bits 
 Per Byte Field), a stop bit is sent to signal the end of a packet. This 
 field specifies how many bits will be used to represent this signal.

EOF Byte: This field 
 represents the character the scale sends at the end of the transmission. 
 Enter the ASCII value of the character in this field.

Translation 
 Parity: This field specifies the type of parity to be used on the 
 data included in the transmission. While parity detects data corruption 
 during transmission, translation parity converts the bytes read from the 
 port in a useable form.

Before you can use the scale to perform an action, the system has to 
 tell it what action to perform. You can define this on the Command Strings 
 Tab. Most of the values you should enter in these fields are in your scale's 
 instruction manual. Ask your system consultant if you have any further 
 questions.

Access the Scale 
 Configuration Window (accessed from the desktop), and click on 
 the Command Strings Tab.

Use the Command String Field 
 to select which command string you want to define.

You can use the "Weight" 
 command string to have the scale weigh an item/shipment.

NOTE: The "Status" 
 and "Zero" command strings are reserved for future use.

Click the Add Button to 
 append a byte to the end of the command string.

Use the Integer Field to 
 indicate the character you want to appear in that position in the command 
 string. Use an ASCII value to represent each character. Each row in the 
 grid represents a position in the command string.

For example, suppose you want to create the following weight command 
 string: W<carriage return>. 
 You would enter the ASCII value    87 
 in the Integer Field. The system will display its corresponding character 
 value in the Character Field (in this case, a    W). 
 Click the Add Button and the system will add another row to the grid. 
 Now enter the value    13 (representing 
 a carriage return) in the Integer Field. The system again displays its 
 corresponding character value in the Character Field (in this case, it 
 is a non-printable character, so it is represented by a generic symbol: 
 a bar).

This setting defines what information the scale will send back to the 
 system. You can tell the system how and what part of the data string to 
 process. You can define this on the Response Strings Tab. Most of the 
 values you should enter in these fields are in your scale's instruction 
 manual. Ask your system consultant if you have any further questions.

Access the Scale 
 Configuration Window (accessed from the desktop), and click on 
 the Response Strings Tab.

Use the Response String Field 
 to select which response string you want to define.

The "Weight" response 
 string defines the significant positions in the set of bytes in 
 the string that the scale sends to the system.

The "Unknown" response 
 string is a string that 
 the scale will send to the system when it does not understand the command 
 that the system sent to it.

Use the Integer Field to indicate the character you want to 
 appear in that position in the response string. Use an ASCII value to 
 represent each character. Each row in the grid represents a position in 
 the response string.

For example, suppose you want to create the following response 
 string:

You would enter the ASCII value 10 
 in the Integer Field. The system will display its corresponding character 
 value in the Character Field (in this case, it is a non-printable character, 
 so it is represented by a generic symbol: a bar). Click the Add Button 
 and the system will add another row to the grid. Now do the same with 
 the remaining integers:    63,    13, and    3.

NOTE: The "Status" 
 and "Zero" response strings are reserved for future use.

Use the Start Position Field and 
 the End Position Field to indicate 
 what characters in the response string the system will recognize as the 
 data you are trying to capture.

For example, when a scale weighs an item, the scale sends back a 
 response string of 16 or more characters, such as the following:

In the above example, <lf> 
 represents a line feed,    <cr> represents 
 a carriage return,    <etx> represents 
 the end of transmission character,    x 
 represents the numbers of the weight,    u represents 
 the units of the weight, and    h represents the 
 status of the scale. In this example, the significant positions of the 
 string are the numbers of the weight, so you would enter a "2" 
 in the Start Position Field and an "8" in the End Position Field.
So, if the scale sent back the following string,
then the system would recognize the weight in pounds as "2.34".

NOTE: The system assumes 
 that the unit of measure configured for use in the system is the same 
 as the scale's unit of measure.

Once you are finished configuring your scale, you need to test the scale's 
 settings before using it in production. You can perform this test on the 
 Scale Connection Test Tab.You will 
 need to save the configuration settings on this window before performing 
 a test. Do this by pressing the Apply Button.
NOTE: Scale Connection Test Tab is only valid when the Generate config file setting is unchecked.

Access the Scale 
 Configuration Window (accessed from the desktop), and click on 
 the Scale Connection Test Tab.

Press the Test Button. The system will begin a test of 
 the scale.

If the test was successful, 
 the system will display the connection details used in the test and the 
 item's weight in the Scale Connection Test Window. Your scale is now ready 
 for use in production.

If the test was not successful, 
 the system will display an error message. Review the test results to determine 
 the error in the Scale Connection Test display. To correct the error, 
 try checking your scale connection and the settings you defined in the 
 previous steps. If that does not work, see your System consultant.

WARNING:If there is a configuration problem with the scale, there 
 is a slight possibility that the system might lock up during the test. 
 If this occurs, restart the application and check the settings that you 
 defined in the previous steps    before 
 repeating the test.

 in the Start Position Field and an "8" in the End Position Field.

                
 

                
So, if the scale sent back the following string,

                
 

                
<lf>0002.34LB<cr><lf>00<cr><etx>

                
 

                
then the system would recognize the weight in pounds as "2.34".

                
 

                
NOTE: The system assumes 
 that the unit of measure configured for use in the system is the same 
 as the scale's unit of measure.

            

        

        
 

        

 5. Scale Connection Test Tab

        
Once you are finished configuring your scale, you need to test the scale's 
 settings before using it in production. You can perform this test on the 
 Scale Connection Test Tab.You will 
 need to save the configuration settings on this window before performing 
 a test. Do this by pressing the Apply Button.

        
 

        
NOTE: Scale Connection Test Tab is only valid when the Generate config file setting is unchecked.

        

            
Access the Scale 
 Configuration Window (accessed from the desktop), and click on 
 the Scale Connection Test Tab.

	 

            

                
Press the Test Button. The system will begin a test of 
 the scale.

                
 

            

            

                

                    
If the test was successful, 
 the system will display the connection details used in the test and the 
 item's weight in the Scale Connection Test Window. Your scale is now ready 
 for use in production.

                    
 

                

                

                    
If the test was not successful, 
 the system will display an error message. Review the test results to determine 
 the error in the Scale Connection Test display. To correct the error, 
 try checking your scale connection and the settings you defined in the 
 previous steps. If that does not work, see your System consultant.

                    
 

                    
WARNING:If there is a configuration problem with the scale, there 
 is a slight possibility that the system might lock up during the test. 
 If this occurs, restart the application and check the settings that you 
 defined in the previous steps    before 
 repeating the test.
